title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop. A Flock Safety camera misread the license plate on Jaclynn Gonzales's car, reading a final digit 2 as 7, and flagged it as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police stopped the vehicle on Calle Duran, handcuffed Jaclynn, 21, and her 12-year-old sister, and placed both in separate police cars before realizing the mistake. Jaclynn asked officers to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but they handcuffed the child instead.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was pulled over and forced to kneel after a similar camera error in April. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The cases are pending.
